question: Rottela Panduga or the Roti Festival is celebrated in which Indian state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Rottela Panduga**, also known as the Roti Festival, is a unique and traditional festival celebrated in the state of **Andhra Pradesh**.

• The festival takes place at the Bara Shaheed Dargah in Nellore, Andhra Pradesh, and is held annually during the month of Muharram.

• It is a time when people from different religious backgrounds come together to exchange **rotis (bread)** as a symbol of their wishes and prayers being fulfilled.

• The festival signifies communal harmony and is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Andhra Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Bara Shaheed Dargah**

• The Bara Shaheed Dargah is a renowned shrine in Nellore, Andhra Pradesh.

• It is dedicated to 12 martyrs who are believed to have died fighting for justice and righteousness.

• The dargah becomes a focal point during the Rottela Panduga, attracting thousands of devotees.

• **Significance of Rottela Panduga**

• The Rottela Panduga is significant for its message of unity and communal harmony, as it brings together people from various communities and religions.

• Devotees believe that exchanging rotis during this festival will fulfill their wishes, whether it be for health, wealth, or other personal desires.

• **Celebration Details**

• The festival involves a series of rituals, including prayers and the exchange of rotis at the Nellore Tank, where devotees congregate.

• People write their wishes on pieces of paper and place them inside the rotis, which are then exchanged with others, symbolizing the sharing of blessings and prayers.
